title: OFT task views vs shared Mirror orthogonal orbit
hypothesis: A shared orthogonal angle template plus scalar task addresses compresses tasks on a common orbit; simple rank-one task-code factorization may provide the same result.
physical_object: One frozen 8x8 linear block and shared orthogonal view family
mirror_coordinate: Six scalar task codes applied to four shared plane-angle generators
controls: full dense OFT Q per task
blockwise OFT plane angles per task
simple rank-one task-code x shared-angle template

task.teacher: Q_t=blockdiag(R(m_t*phi_j)); task m and shared phi vary by seed

optimization.fit: least squares task maps; nonlinear least squares for shared template/address

paid_objects: Mirror shared angle template and task codes

compute.active_compute_proxy: dense Q application and linear block multiply; transform time reported separately

success_gate: At least 3/4 fresh: Mirror MSE <=1.10x full OFT, <=80% its bytes, orthogonality/cycle <1e-10 and lower bytes than simple rank-one angle factorization.
failure_gate: Mirror MSE >1.25x OFT on >=3/4 or no byte-quality improvement over simple factorized angle control.
development_amendment: Development revealed Mirror is exactly the ordinary rank-one factorization of task-by-plane angle matrix. Before fresh access, serialize the simple rank-one control and Mirror with identical packed tensors; archive-header differences are not model compression.
amended_success_gate: Report actual byte/quality frontier. No Mirror-specific PASS is possible unless it improves over the exact rank-one control under identical state encoding; functional equality is reported as a negative Mirror-specific result.
protocol_variant_note: A separate trained cross-over against dense OFT is retained under protocol_variants/task_views_vs_dense_oft; it did not include the exact simple rank-one control and is not pooled.
